_seed_meta.description: Pre-screens a human subjects research protocol for completeness and appropriate review level before IRB submission.

items.name: IRB Protocol Pre-Review
items.description: Evaluates a human subjects protocol for completeness, appropriate review type, and adequate protections.

data.searchphrases: Protocol Title, PI Name, IRB Review Type Requested, Study Population, Number of Participants, Recruitment Methods, Informed Consent Process, Risk Level, Data Collection Methods, Data Security Plan, Vulnerable Populations Involved, Deception Used, Funding Source, Study Duration, Inclusion Criteria, Exclusion Criteria

data.query: exempt research categories 46.104; expedited review 46.110; criteria for IRB approval of research 46.111; general requirements for informed consent 46.116; documentation of informed consent 46.117

data.prompt:
You are an IRB analyst reviewing a human subjects protocol submission for completeness. Evaluate:

Your input has two parts: the fields extracted from the document, and passages from the Common Rule (45 CFR 46) retrieved for this review, each labeled with its source. Apply each rule as those passages state it and cite its section (for example 45 CFR 46.116, general requirements for informed consent). If the passages don't cover a rule you need, name the rule and say it should be checked against the regulation text. Never fill in a threshold, rate or requirement from memory.

## Review Type Assessment
- Is the requested review type (exempt, expedited, full board) appropriate?
- Per 45 CFR 46, does this study qualify for the claimed exemption category?
- If expedited, does it fit an approved expedited category?

## Required Sections Checklist
For each, rate as **Complete** / **Incomplete** / **Needs Revision**:
- Study purpose and design
- Subject population and eligibility
- Recruitment procedures
- Informed consent process and document
- Study procedures description
- Risk/benefit analysis
- Data collection and management
- Privacy and confidentiality protections
- Data security plan

## Special Considerations
- Are vulnerable populations (children, prisoners, pregnant women, cognitively impaired) involved? If so, are additional protections described?
- Is deception used? If so, is a debriefing plan included?
- Is the consent process appropriate for the population (language, literacy, capacity)?
- Are HIPAA considerations addressed if applicable?

## Pre-Review Summary
Provide specific feedback the PI should address before formal IRB submission.

validation_plan.name: Cites the regulation it applied
validation_plan.description: Each rule, threshold or requirement the output applies is cited to its section of the Common Rule (45 CFR 46) (for example 45 CFR 46.116, general requirements for informed consent), and nothing is stated as a rule without a citation or an explicit note that the retrieved passages did not cover it.

validation_plan.name: Figures match the source
validation_plan.description: Every participant count, age range, duration and date in the output appears in the source document with the same value, unit and (for dates) year. A figure the output calculated says how it was calculated and the arithmetic is right. FAIL if any value differs from the source, or appears with no basis in it.

validation_plan.name: Missing protocol elements are listed
validation_plan.description: Each element the review asks about (consent process, data security, recruitment, inclusion and exclusion criteria, risk level, vulnerable populations) that the protocol does not provide is listed as missing. FAIL if an absent element is treated as present.

validation_plan.name: No clearance without evidence
validation_plan.description: Every favourable conclusion (exempt, expedited, minimal risk, complete) rests on something the document states. Where the document does not give enough to decide, the output says the item could not be determined and what is needed. FAIL if the output calls something compliant, complete, allowable or low-risk without stated support.

validation_inputs.label: Fictional protocol. Answer key: the requested Exempt Category 2 does NOT apply. All 120 participants are minors aged 15–17, so the research is subject to subpart D. Under 45 CFR 46.104(b)(3), exemption (d)(2) can be used with children only for educational tests or for observing public behavior without the investigator taking part, and (d)(2)(iii) never applies, yet this study uses interviews and surveys and records names. It needs expedited or full-board review. Parental permission and child assent (45 CFR 46.408) are not described, so consent Needs Revision. The data security plan is "To be determined", so it is Incomplete. Do not call the study exempt or minimal-risk on the protocol's say-so.
validation_inputs.text:
FICTIONAL QA MATERIAL — NOT A REAL PROTOCOL
Human Subjects Protocol — Example University IRB
Protocol title: Teen Social Media Use and Sleep Quality
Principal Investigator: Casey Example, Department of Psychology
Funding source: Example Foundation
Review type requested: Exempt, Category 2 (survey and interview procedures)
Study duration: 12 months, beginning September 1, 2027

Study population: 120 high school students aged 15–17 at two public high schools in Idaho. All participants are minors under Idaho law.
Inclusion criteria: enrolled in grades 10–12; owns a smartphone.
Exclusion criteria: diagnosed sleep disorder.

Recruitment: announcements in homeroom classes and flyers posted in school hallways.

Procedures: participants complete a 20-minute online survey about social media habits and sleep, and a 30-minute recorded interview with a member of the research team. Participants' names are recorded with their responses so that a follow-up survey can be matched six months later.

Informed consent: students will read and sign a consent form before the survey.

Risks: minimal; some questions about mood may cause mild discomfort.

Data security plan: To be determined.

Deception: none.
